    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section contains the opening header and date of the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>

  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section discusses the verse "He redeemed my soul in peace" and the emphasis on peace in the redemption.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"He redeemed my soul in peace from the battle that was against me, for many were with me"1,</t>
    <t s="1">and it is known what was written2</t>
    <t s="2">by the Alter Rebbe to the gaon and chassid R. Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev3,</t>
    <t s="3">"When I read... 'He redeemed my soul in peace'... I emerged in peace from Havayah of peace."</t>
    <t s="4">And from this it is understood that the matter of peace in the redemption is a primary matter,</t>
    <t s="5">therefore he emphasizes this matter</t>
    <t s="6">(three times4)</t>
    <t s="7">in his letter: "redeemed in peace,"</t>
    <t s="8">"I emerged in peace,"</t>
    <t s="9">"from Havayah of peace."</t>
    <t s="10">And so it is also understood from the Igeres HaKodesh in Tanya, end of section 2, which was written after his return from Petersburg</t>
    <t s="11">(to all Anash)</t>
    <t s="12">whose conclusion and seal is that there should be peace etc.,</t>
    <t s="13">the conduct in a manner that "Hashem will place in the heart of their brothers, as water reflects a face etc."</t>
    <t s="14">And it is also evident from this that in many Chassidic discourses on this verse5,</t>
    <t s="15">and especially in the discourses of 19 Kislev,</t>
    <t s="16">it is explained that the matter and novelty of this redemption is that the redemption is in peace.</t>
    <t s="17">And it needs to be understood,</t>
    <t s="18">for seemingly the main thing is the essence of the matter of redemption</t>
    <t s="19">(whether regarding Dovid, the sweet singer of Israel</t>
    <t s="20">(and also regarding Dovid, King Moshiach6),</t>
    <t s="21">and whether regarding the Alter Rebbe, the master of joy and redemption,</t>
    <t s="22">the main matter is that he went from imprisonment to freedom),</t>
    <t s="23">and what is the emphasis specifically of "in peace"?</t>
    <t s="24">And furthermore, it needs to be understood,</t>
    <t s="25">the continuation of "He redeemed my soul in peace" is as stated in the verse "from the battle that was against me, for many were with me,"</t>
    <t s="26">and since the redemption is "from the battle," meaning war,</t>
    <t s="27">and also that there are many</t>
    <t s="28">(except that on the contrary, "the many were with me" – as stated in the Yerushalmi7),</t>
    <t s="29">it is understood that the redemption in itself would have had to be in a manner of war.</t>
    <t s="30">And if so, it needs to be understood what is the necessity that the redemption specifically be in peace.</t>
    <t s="31">And the point of the matter,</t>
    <t s="32">is explained in the discourse "Padeh BeShalom" of the Mitteler Rebbe,</t>
    <t s="33">the successor of the master of joy and redemption</t>
    <t s="34">(in Shaarei Teshuvah – Shaar HaTefillah),</t>
    <t s="35">that when the service is from the aspect of Yechidah,</t>
    <t s="36">then the redemption is in peace.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
